This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=katl

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the National Weather Service and multiple models places Austin’s August 31 high in the upper 90s to low 100s, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting on 98–101°F.** Official point forecasts from the Austin/San Antonio NWS office indicate a high near 101°F under mostly sunny skies, with south-southeast winds of 5–10 mph and heat indices reaching 104°F. Other sources, including WeatherBug and local analyses, converge on 98–99°F, reflecting minor model spread typical of late-summer high-pressure dominance over central Texas.

This range sits modestly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of ~95°F for the date, driven by persistent warm advection and limited cloud cover rather than any acute heat wave. No significant frontal passages or tropical moisture intrusions are expected today, keeping precipitation chances near zero and allowing full solar heating. **Trader consensus centers on 78-79°F (47.5% implied probability) and 80-81°F (30%) as the leading outcomes for Los Angeles’s official high on August 31, 2026.** These bins align with National Weather Service and LAX-focused forecasts projecting highs in the upper 70s to low-to-mid 80s under partly cloudy to sunny conditions.

The primary driver is the recent moderation following a prolonged late-August heat wave. High pressure over the Southwest had produced multiple days above 85–90°F (with peaks near 90°F around August 27), but stronger onshore flow and a deeper marine layer have returned, capping coastal and valley maxima. This typical late-summer pattern—enhanced sea breezes and low stratus/fog in the morning—prevents further intensification and favors readings near the long-term August average high of ~77–85°F at key stations.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Hong Kong’s highest temperature on September 1 centers on the 29–30°C range (combined ~71.5% implied probability), driven by the official Hong Kong Observatory forecast of 26–30°C amid the influence of Tropical Cyclone Sadul and the northeast monsoon.**

As of late August 31, Sadul is tracking across the northern South China Sea toward eastern Guangdong, enhancing wind shear and moisture that favor widespread cloud cover, squally showers, and thunderstorms. These conditions limit solar heating and promote evaporative cooling, keeping daytime maxima from exceeding the upper 20s to low 30s. Multiple numerical models and ensemble guidance converge on highs near 29–30°C (roughly 84–86°F), consistent with climatological early-September averages around 29.6°C, though localized heavy rain could suppress the peak by 1–2°C in some districts.

The near-even split between 29°C and 30°C reflects residual uncertainty in rainfall timing and intensity: lighter or later showers would allow brief afternoon warming toward 30°C, while persistent cloud and downpours favor a 29°C ceiling. Lower-probability outcomes (28°C at 11%, 31°C at 10%) hinge on greater model divergence in storm placement or unexpected clearing. With resolution occurring within hours, traders are weighting the latest HKO guidance and short-range model runs most heavily.

As of late August 31, the India Meteorological Department reports ongoing rainfall across Uttar Pradesh, including yellow alerts for heavy rain and totals nearing seasonal norms (~500 mm in Lucknow). This pattern typically persists into early September, suppressing maximum temperatures through reduced solar insolation, evaporative cooling from precipitation, and elevated moisture levels that limit diurnal warming.

Short-range model guidance and climatological analogs show expected highs clustered in the 29–32°C range: patchy rain or thunderstorms on September 2 favor the lower end (around 29–30°C), while any temporary breaks in cloud cover could allow brief spikes toward 31–32°C. Historical early-September averages hover near 33–34°C under drier conditions, but the current active monsoon phase—marked by cyclonic systems and strong moisture influx—shifts probabilities downward. Resolution hinges on precise rainfall timing, intensity, and local wind patterns from the India Meteorological Department and global models, with the latest updates likely to refine trader-implied odds clustered around 29–31°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon flow combined with scattered thunderstorms and an approaching tropical depression is expected to limit peak solar heating in Manila on September 2, keeping the daily maximum temperature tightly clustered around 30–32 °C.** 

Official PAGASA guidance and multiple numerical models (including GFS-derived products) show widespread cloud cover, 60–90 % rain probabilities, and southwesterly winds of 15–25 mph through the day. These conditions reduce incoming shortwave radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, preventing temperatures from exceeding the recent observed high of 31.5 °C (recorded August 31 at the Science Garden station). 

Historical September averages for Metro Manila hover near 31 °C, but the active monsoon and potential indirect effects from Tropical Depression Pilandok (located east of northern Luzon) introduce additional moisture and convective activity that typically shave 1–2 °C off clear-sky maxima. 

The near-even market shares between 31 °C (24.5 %) and 32 °C (24.0 %) reflect this narrow uncertainty band: small differences in the timing or intensity of afternoon convection—driven by model spread in boundary-layer moisture and wind shear—can easily shift the observed peak by a single degree. Lower-probability outcomes below 30 °C or above 33 °C would require either unusually persistent heavy rain or unexpected clearing, both of which current ensemble guidance assigns low likelihood. Updated PAGASA bulletins and the next model runs in the next 24–48 hours will provide the clearest signals for traders.

This setup favors efficient boundary-layer heating with minimal cloud cover or precipitation to limit surface temperatures, consistent with the warmer-than-average September outlook from NOAA. Trader sentiment across the 77–96°F+ bins reflects residual uncertainty in 48–72-hour model spreads on wind mixing and any late-day convective development, which could shift peak readings by several degrees.
